atomic_claim: In preregistered online survey experiments in the United States and Brazil, assignment to factual messages about election-security procedures generally improved self-reported election confidence and factual accuracy and reduced election-fraud beliefs immediately after exposure; persistence was mixed.
endpoint: Self-reported election confidence, perceived prevalence and effects of election fraud, and accuracy or discernment for election-procedure statements.
notes: Bounded to static forced-exposure messages and survey outcomes; no evidence on assistant grounding, voting-access errors, turnout, abstention, administrative disenfranchisement, correction reach, or electoral behaviour.

atomic_claim: In a 40-participant United States within-subject field experiment using injected cookie-consent notices during normal browsing, removing the first-page Reject all button increased acceptance by 22.0 percentage points for barrier notices and 23.1 percentage points for banner notices.
endpoint: Binary acceptance of injected cookie-consent notices under a first-page button-prominence manipulation.
notes: The study did not test a regulatory ban or causally estimate whether button prominence changed alignment with participants' ideal privacy preferences, actual data disclosure, legal compliance, political behaviour, or agency transfer; the published confidence interval for the banner estimate is internally inconsistent.

atomic_claim: Among 1,037,113 observed appearances of 136,924 duplicated multimedia items that received at least one Forwarded Many Times label in 1,101 public Brazilian political WhatsApp groups from June to October 2022, 612,855 appearances (59%) did not carry that label.
endpoint: Share of observed duplicate-multimedia appearances lacking an FMT label, conditional on the item having at least one FMT-labelled appearance.
notes: Descriptive result for selected public political groups; no counterfactual estimate of effects on cost, delay, reach, virality, encryption properties, or harm. The 59% is not a platform-wide false-negative rate.

atomic_claim: Short technique-based inoculation videos increased United States participants' immediate recognition of the specific manipulation techniques taught, including a small recognition effect in a YouTube ad study measured within 24 hours.
endpoint: Immediate recognition of specifically taught manipulation techniques.
notes: Six online randomized experiments and one YouTube field study support this bounded endpoint; they do not establish durability beyond 24 hours, actual sharing, transfer to untaught techniques or cultures, election-specific effects, pluralism, reflective agency, or agency transfer.

atomic_claim: In offline experiments on MovieLens and Google Location data, performance-based minimisation reduced the per-user ratings available to recommender systems while producing algorithm-, metric-, and user-dependent quality losses.
endpoint: Offline recommender-system RMSE and NDCG under reduced per-user rating histories.
notes: Supports bounded technical feasibility of data minimisation in two recommender datasets; does not test assistant memory, deletion completeness, intimate manipulation, dependency, or real-user outcomes.

atomic_claim: In a 2019 exercise of GDPR Article 20 across four consumer IoT systems, researchers received relevant personal data in three of four exercises; none enabled import into a second provider or direct provider-to-provider transmission.
endpoint: Successful receipt of relevant personal data, import into a second provider, and direct transmission across four Article 20 portability exercises.
notes: In the fourth exercise Amazon returned data associated with another account. This negative implementation evidence from a four-system snapshot does not test assistant-state portability, switching time, useful context transferred, redress, lock-in, or agency outcomes.

atomic_claim: As of 2026-08-13, publication of an Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard record is mandatory as an administrative policy for in-scope United Kingdom central-government organisations using Beta/Pilot or Production algorithmic tools that meet the public-effect or direct-public-interaction criteria; it is recommended rather than mandatory outside that scope, and exemptions apply.
notes: The mandate is an administrative policy, not a general statute; scope and exemptions must be assessed for each organisation and tool.

atomic_claim: As of 2026-08-13, the Digital Markets Act expressly includes virtual assistants as a core platform service category, but gatekeeper duties apply only when the European Commission has designated the undertaking for the specified service.
notes: Virtual-assistant status alone does not trigger DMA duties; designation and the scope of the designation decision are controlling.
